info.title: mc8yp HTTP API
info.description:
Auxiliary REST surface of the mc8yp Cumulocity MCP microservice.

This spec intentionally documents only the non-MCP HTTP routes (`/refresh-apis`, `/resolve-mcp-servers`, `/health`). The MCP protocol itself is served at `POST /mcp` over JSON-RPC and is **not** documented here — MCP clients discover tools and prompts via the MCP `tools/list` / `prompts/list` flow, not via OpenAPI. If you are an agent reading this through `serviceSpecs['mc8yp-server']`, you are talking to mc8yp through mc8yp; do not call `/service/mc8yp-server/mcp` from inside `execute`.

The primary use cases for this spec are letting an agent trigger a fresh API discovery in mc8yp itself after subscribing or unsubscribing a microservice in the tenant, and letting a management UI resolve and check external MCP server configuration before storing it.

post.summary: Bust the API discovery cache and re-run discovery for the calling tenant.
post.description:
Resolves the tenant from the caller's `Authorization` header (or session cookie), busts the per-tenant discovery cache, and synchronously re-runs Cumulocity application + OpenAPI spec discovery using the microservice's service user for that tenant. Returns the freshly discovered spec metadata.

Use this after a new microservice has been subscribed in the tenant — otherwise discovered specs stay cached for 30 minutes.

401.description: No Authorization header or session cookie was provided.

400.description: Could not resolve the calling tenant via `/tenant/currentTenant`.

403.description: Tenant is not subscribed to this microservice.

500.description: Discovery failed for an unexpected reason.

post.summary: Resolve and check external MCP server configuration before it is used.
post.description:
Answers the three questions a caller building the `mc8yp-mcp-server` header cannot answer itself: **which namespace** each entry would be mounted under (derived from its free-form `name` by the same sanitization a Cumulocity contextPath gets, so `MaStR registry` becomes `MaStR_registry`), **whether that namespace is available** (reserved names, namespaces already held by this tenant, and duplicates within the request), and **whether the server answers** — the MCP handshake runs with the entry's own credentials, exactly as it would at runtime, and the tool list it returns is what the agent would see.

Why this matters: at runtime a tenant namespace always wins a collision and the external server is then **silently skipped**, so the operator believes the agent has a namespace it does not have. This route turns that into a visible `namespace-taken` verdict at configuration time.

The entry shape is the header's, except that `name` may be free-form here. It is a POST with a body rather than a GET reading the header because the entries carry credentials and the candidate is typically not configured on any connection yet.

**The namespace does not become dynamic.** The header contract stays strict and verbatim: resolve a display name once, store the `namespace` you got back, and send that from then on. Nothing is persisted here — mc8yp holds no external server configuration of its own.

Handshakes are neither served from nor written to the per-session tool-list cache, so the answer always reflects the credentials as sent.

200.description: One resolution per submitted entry, in the order they were sent. A 200 does NOT mean every entry is usable — read each `status`.

400.description: Body was not an object carrying a `servers` array. Per-entry problems are reported as `invalid` inside a 200, not here.

401.description: No Authorization header or session cookie was provided.

500.description: Resolution failed for an unexpected reason.

get.description: Returns the static string `OK` with a 200 status when the process is alive. No authentication required.

tenantUrl.description: Base URL of the Cumulocity tenant the microservice is deployed against.

tenantId.description: Cumulocity tenant ID resolved from the caller's auth.

installedContextPaths.description: Context paths of every Cumulocity application currently subscribed by the tenant, regardless of whether the application exposes an OpenAPI spec.

discovered.description: One entry per application that exposes a reachable OpenAPI spec. Paths in each spec have already been prefixed with the application's service URL prefix.

specLabel.description: Human-readable label of the spec entry. Equals the application name for single-spec applications.

pathCount.description: Number of paths declared by the spec after the service-prefix rewrite.

servers.description: Candidate entries. An empty array is valid and resolves to an empty result.

ExternalMcpServerCandidate.description: One external MCP server as an operator configures it — the `mc8yp-mcp-server` entry shape, except that `name` may be free-form because the namespace is derived from it here.

name.description: Display name. Sanitized into the namespace: spaces, hyphens and dots become underscores, other non-word characters are dropped, a leading digit gains an underscore, and a JavaScript keyword gains a trailing one. A name that is already a valid identifier passes through unchanged.

url.description: Absolute http/https MCP endpoint, used as provided.

token.description: Bearer shorthand: sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the external server. Not persisted and not logged.

headers.description: Extra request headers, applied after `token` so an explicit `authorization` entry replaces the bearer shorthand.

description.description: Shown to the agent in the namespace overview; falls back to the server's own `instructions`.

tenantUrl.description: Base URL of the Cumulocity tenant the microservice is deployed against.

tenantId.description: Tenant resolved from the caller's auth. Absent when resolution failed.

tenantNamespaces.description: Every namespace this tenant already occupies (core plus one per available service) — the set an external namespace has to fit around. **`null` means the check did not run** (see `warnings`), so a namespace reported free may still be taken at runtime.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems that limit how much of the answer can be trusted. Empty on a fully checked response.

servers.description: One entry per submitted server, same order.

name.description: The `name` as submitted, echoed so results can be matched to input.

namespace.description: The namespace this entry would be mounted under — **the value to store and to send in the `mc8yp-mcp-server` header from now on**. Empty when the entry carried no usable name.

status.description:
The one field to branch on.
- `ok` — valid, namespace free, server answered.
- `invalid` — the entry is malformed; sending it in the header would fail the whole request with a 400.
- `namespace-taken` — well-formed, but the namespace is claimed, so at runtime this server is skipped and the agent silently would not have it. Rename it.
- `unreachable` — well-formed and free, but the handshake failed. mc8yp retries on the next codemode call, so this may be transient.

reason.description: Why the status is not `ok`, phrased for an operator. Absent when it is.

namespaceTakenBy.description: Who holds the namespace: a sandbox global (`codemode`, `docs`, `sandbox`, `c8y`, `cumulocity`), a namespace of this tenant, or an earlier entry in the same request. Only set for `namespace-taken`.

server.description: The downstream server's own handshake identity. Present when it answered.

instructions.description: The server's `instructions`, which mc8yp shows the agent when the entry has no `description`.

tools.description: The tools the agent would get from this namespace. Present whenever the handshake succeeded — including for `namespace-taken`, so an operator renaming the entry already knows the URL and credential are right.

name.description: Tool name as advertised by the server.

description.description: The tool's description, or its title when it has none.
